primary_question: Does a learned structural representation reduce actual structural execution while preserving capability relative to exhaustive CASM execution?

primary_endpoint.name: selective_execution_work_fraction_at_capability
primary_endpoint.criterion: At a population level M, an arm is capability-eligible when selective semantic success divided by exhaustive semantic success is >= 0.80. Report the minimum execution-work fraction among eligible budgets; no winner is selected across representations.

structural_tower.description: Frozen CASM-S structural representation plus learned query tower and candidate projection.
structural_tower.trainable_parameter_budget: shared fixed query MLP and 32x32 candidate projection

summary_tower.description: Hand-designed public node-local structural summary with the same tower architecture and trainable parameter budget.

random.description: Uniform candidate order; no learned parameters.

exhaustive.description: Execute all M candidates with the same CASM-S evaluator; capability ceiling/control.

data_protocol.primary_eval_distribution: same generator distribution with unseen exact structures and unseen truth tables; candidate pools are generated independently of router-visible support examples
data_protocol.secondary_eval_distribution: held-out NOT->XOR structural role-pair; training excludes that role-pair

leakage_rules: Router input contains only public support input/output examples and candidate public structural descriptors.
Target index, target record ID, full candidate truth tables, true wiring, true edges, verifier output, and outcome are evaluator-only.
CASM-S structural encoder receives nodes, depth, position, arity, and existence only; true edges are not passed into routing.
Candidate semantic success is verified from executed outputs against public task examples, not descriptor equality.
A candidate is not marked negative unless its executed outputs fail at least one public task example.
Candidate pool construction must not condition decoy inclusion on router-visible support examples.
Verifier-only input/output examples are disjoint from router-visible support examples and are not passed to routing.
Opaque task addresses are derived only from router-visible support examples and contain no target index, target ID, or hidden verifier data.
All 12 remaining truth-table rows are verifier-only; together with the four router-visible rows they cover the complete 4-input Boolean truth table.
Primary evaluation target truth tables are absent from router training as well as target structures.

execution_work_contract.gate_evaluations: number of candidate edges scored by CASM-S
execution_work_contract.edge_message_operations: number of candidate-edge message aggregation operations
execution_work_contract.structural_node_operations: number of active non-input nodes executed

statistical_contract.primary_estimate: pooled trial-level semantic success and execution-work fraction
statistical_contract.multiple_comparisons: descriptive across M and budgets; no global arm winner claim
statistical_contract.training_selection: no held-out outcome used to choose training hyperparameters or arm

promotion_rule: CASM exhaustive capability >= 0.80 on the primary eval condition
router target IDs are absent from runtime inputs
selective execution work is measured from actual CASM operations
capability retention and execution work are both reported
no asymptotic scaling claim from finite M

persistent_experience.task_state: opaque task address resolves public task examples
persistent_experience.commit_rule: only candidates that pass all public task examples after actual CASM-S execution can be written as experience
persistent_experience.intervening_writes: unrelated task records are inserted before anchor replay
persistent_experience.replay_metric: compare routing and adaptive execution before and after verified experience

title: M2 actual CASM selective execution
question: Does a learned structural representation reduce actual structural execution while preserving capability relative to exhaustive CASM execution?
hypothesis: Selective structural routing should preserve useful task capability while reducing actual CASM-S execution work relative to exhaustive execution, under unique candidates and held-out structure.

arms.name: structural_tower
arms.intervention: frozen CASM-S structural representation plus learned query-to-structure tower

arms.name: summary_tower
arms.intervention: matched learned query-to-summary tower using a fixed public structural summary

arms.name: exhaustive
arms.intervention: execute every candidate with the same pinned CASM-S evaluator

endpoints.name: selective_execution_work_fraction_at_capability
endpoints.description: Minimum selective CASM-S execution work fraction among registered budgets with at least 0.80 semantic capability retention versus exhaustive execution at the same M.

decision_rule.condition: At each registered M, at least one structural_tower budget satisfies capability retention >= 0.80 versus exhaustive execution.
decision_rule.licenses: bounded evidence that selective structural routing can preserve capability while reducing actual CASM-S work under the registered workload.
decision_rule.does_not_license: asymptotic sublinear scaling, universal program retrieval, language intelligence, or hardware speedup.

decision_rule.condition: No registered selective budget meets capability retention >= 0.80 at a registered M.
decision_rule.licenses: the registered selective mechanism does not meet the capability-constrained execution criterion at that M.
decision_rule.does_not_license: a general impossibility result for selective structural computation.

decision_rule.condition: Exhaustive CASM-S semantic success is below 0.80 at a registered M.
decision_rule.licenses: the downstream executor ceiling is insufficient for a capability-relative selective verdict at that M.
decision_rule.does_not_license: a routing failure attribution at that M.

held_constant: pinned CASM-S commit and Python 3.12 runtime
four input Boolean programs on a fixed 10-node substrate
four router-visible examples and twelve verifier-only truth-table rows
target ID, target index, true wiring, and hidden target descriptor absent from router inputs
unique candidate structures and unique complete truth tables
router architecture and trainable parameter count matched between structural and summary arms
adaptive execution rule fixed before evaluation outcomes
